hints: Focus on what makes an SN2 mechanism special compared to SN1, especially the timing of bond breaking and bond making.
Look at the product name, propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$), and ask yourself which atom of $\text{CN}^-$ must form the new bond to carbon.
Combine those two ideas: a one-step direct attack with no carbocation, plus the atom that gives a C-C bond, to pick the correct description.
walkthrough:
**Recall what SN2 means**

Think of SN2 as one smooth, concerted step. The nucleophile attacks as the leaving group leaves. There is no carbocation intermediate at all.

Reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Br}^-$$

**Decide which end of cyanide attacks**

Cyanide, $\text{CN}^-$, is ambident. It has a lone pair on both C and N. But the product here is propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$, which has a new C-C bond.

That tells us attack must happen through the carbon lone pair, not the nitrogen lone pair. Attack through N would give an isocyanide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-N}\equiv\text{C}$.

**Put SN2 together with the correct attack**

So we need direct attack by the C lone pair on the $\delta+$ carbon of the $\text{C-Br}$ bond, from the backside, while $\text{Br}^-$ leaves. This matches a correct SN2 description with no carbocation formed first.

options.A: Correct. This describes SN2 perfectly: concerted backside attack by the nucleophile on the carbon of the C-Br bond, and attack by C of CN- gives the observed nitrile product with a new C-C bond.
options.B: Incorrect. It correctly identifies C as the attacking atom, but a carbocation forming first is SN1, not SN2. Bromoethane is primary and reacts by the concerted SN2 pathway with no carbocation intermediate.
options.C: Incorrect. Attack on the C-Br carbon is correct for SN2, but attack by N would form a C-N bond and give an isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$), not the stated product propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$).
options.D: Incorrect on both counts. Attack by N would give the wrong product, and attack on a pre-formed carbocation describes SN1, not the concerted SN2 mechanism asked for.
